 RJ Barrett put up 12 points (5-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, seven assists, two steals, and a block in loss on Wednesday to the Celtics. 
 RJ will have games where he will take a bunch of shots and miss a lot of them. The Raptors were without Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes in this one, so the Raptors needed the offense. The Celtics did a good job guarding him which ended up being the difference between a win and a loss. He’ll have better games from the field, and enjoy the peripheral stats you got in this one. 
 -  Brian Taylor

 RJ Barrett supplied 27 points (9-of-21 FGs, 9-of-11 FTs), seven rebounds and five assists over 37 minutes to propel the Raptors to a 121-107 win over the Bucks on Friday. 
 Barrett was tasked with shouldering more of the scoring workload in this one with Kawhi Leonard (knee), Scottie Barnes (groin) and Immanuel Quickly (hamstring) out due to injuries. The 26-year-old hoisted a team-leading 21 shot attempts and got to the free-throw line regularly against a struggling Milwaukee squad. He’ll continue to be relevant for fantasy managers as Toronto’s primary offensive catalyst until the rest of their starting lineup gets healthy. 
 RJ Barrett 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #9 
 The Toronto Raptors will start Jamal Shead, Ja’Kobe Walter, RJ Barrett, Collin Murray-Boyles, and Jakob Poeltl against the Bucks on Friday. 
 Immanuel Quickley (hamstring) and Scottie Barnes (adductor, groin) will not play in Friday’s game, so the Raptors replaced them with Jamal Shead and Jakob Poeltl. If either of them are available in redraft leagues, they are worth a stream for Friday. Shead would be the priority over Poeltl given the fact that Shead will have the ball more, but most of his value comes from assists. 
 RJ Barrett 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #9 
 RJ Barrett put up 22 points (7-of-17 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, and three 3-pointers in 128-109 loss to the Nuggets. 
 Barrett led the team in shot attempts in this game and he did a good job scoring the ball. On the season, he’s averaging 20.9 points, 6 rebounds, 3.9 assists, 0.5 steals, and 0.5 blocks, shooting 48.1% from the field, 59.5% from the free throw line, and 31.8% from three. Outside of the free throw percentage, he’s been great for where he was selected in redraft leagues. There’s even room for him to get better once he starts hitting more of his free throws. 
 RJ Barrett 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #9 
 RJ Barrett tallied 26 points (10-of-19 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Clippers. 
 Barrett scored 16 points in the first half of Monday’s game, shooting 7-of-9 from the field. The overall stat line was good, except for one category: free-throw percentage. Barrett is shooting a career-worst 58.8 percent from the charity stripe this season, a number that has done his category league value no favors. That said, Barrett is a career 69.5 percent shooter, so it may not be too surprising that he’s started slowly in that regard. 
 RJ Barrett 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #9 
 RJ Barrett accumulated 22 points (9-of-18 FGs), 10 rebounds, five assists and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers. 
 Barrett has scored at least 20 points in three of his last four games, a stretch that coincides with the Raptors’ loss of Kawhi Leonard to a knee injury. While he didn’t record any defensive stats on Sunday, fantasy managers will be pleased with Barrett’s double-double, his first of the season, and the assists. The Raptors play three games next week, starting with the Clippers on Monday. 
 RJ Barrett 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #9 
 RJ Barrett with a monster 25 points (9-of-8 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), nine rebounds, six assists, a steal and three 3-pointers on Wednesday against the Magic. 
 RJ Barrett took the shots early in this game in the first game without Kawhi and was efficient from the field. Notably, he was on the exercise bike at multiple points in this game, so it could be something to monitor. If you got RJ Barrett in fantasy, you should be really happy about what he’s been doing. He won’t get you many defensive numbers but he will certainly score, and get you some rebounds. There’s an opportunity with Kawhi out, so there could be room to sell-high if someone gives you a good offer. 
 Ja'Kobe Walter 
 TOR 
 Guard 
 #14 
 The Toronto Raptors will start Immanuel Quickley, Ja’Kobe Walter, RJ Barrett, Scottie Barnes, and Jakob Poeltl against the Magic on Friday. 
 Kawhi Leonard is out with knee soreness, so Ja’Kobe Walter will get the start against the Magic. He’s useful if you need some points and 3’s but he likely will not be much more than a deeper league guy. Look for Barnes, Quickley, and Barrett to pick up the slack without Kawhi. 
 RJ Barrett 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #9 
 RJ Barrett finished Sunday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 20 points (9-of-21 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, two assists and three steals. 
 Barrett helped keep the Raptors within striking distance of the Timberwolves in the first half, scoring 14 points. Unfortunately for him, he went cold in the third quarter, along with the rest of the Raptors, shooting 1-of-5 from the field. Toronto was outscored 35-15 as Kawhi Leonard’s absence and Scottie Barnes’ 0-of-12 shooting caught up to them. Barrett and the Raptors will look to bounce back on Wednesday against the Magic. 
 RJ Barrett 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #9 
 RJ Barrett played great with 23 points (9-of-16 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), nine rebounds, four assists, a block and a three in 34 minutes. 
 We got one of RJ’s good games in this one. He’s gotten much better with peripheral stats since getting to the Raptors. There will be bad games where you will get frustrated with the shot chucking when he’s missing shots, but for now, if you have RJ, you’re feeling good after this performance. 
 RJ Barrett 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #9 
 RJ Barrett amassed 20 points (8-of-14 FGs, 4-of-7 FTs), four rebounds and three assists in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls. 
 After scoring six points on 3-of-8 shooting in the first half, Barrett scored 10 in the third quarter alone. He shot well on Wednesday, making just over half his shots, and he also posted solid rebound and assist numbers. Most encouraging were the 14 shots, possibly a sign that Barrett’s volume won’t suffer much with Kawhi Leonard back in Toronto. Barrett has long offered better value in points leagues than category leagues, and that’s unlikely to change in 2026-27.
